summary: An excerpt from a novel's Book 1, part 153, in which the first-person narrator Marcus Yallow reflects on a sexual encounter with Ange, describing mixed feelings of change and intimacy afterward. The passage then shifts to his routine of checking email, dealing with spam and joe-jobbing targeting his Swedish mailbox, and sorting encrypted messages from his web of trust, one of which is encrypted only to his public key and is about to be read.
one_line: Marcus Yallow reflects on his intimate moment with Ange, then sorts spam and encrypted messages, ending on a mysterious message encrypted to his key alone.
key_facts: The narrator Marcus Yallow says the sexual experience with Ange was nothing like he expected, with parts better and parts much worse.
Afterwards Ange was grinning while fat tears rolled down her cheeks, and she whispered to Marcus Yallow, "You're a good man, Marcus Yallow."
Marcus wrapped the condom in kleenex, wound it with toilet paper, and stuck it deep into the trash-can.
Ange was playing with her Xbox while sitting up in bed, and she pointed at Marcus's Xbox on the floor to signal him to log in.
Marcus's Swedish mailbox was repeatedly "joe-jobbed," meaning it was used as the return address for spam sent to hundreds of millions of Internet accounts.
Marcus suspected the DHS might be trying to overwhelm his mailbox, though he also considered that it could just be people pranking him.
The Pirate Party's email service gave anyone who wanted it 500 gigabytes of email storage and had pretty good filters.
Marcus kept a separate mailbox for messages encrypted to his public key, since these were likely Xnet-related and possibly sensitive.
Spammers had not yet realized that using public keys would make their junk mail more plausible.
There were a couple dozen encrypted messages from people in the web of trust, including links to videos and pictures of DHS abuses.
One message was encrypted only to Marcus's public key, meaning no one else could read it.
